items.title: feat(core): support configurable string normalization
items.body:
Follow-up to discussion #8165.

Adds opt-in string normalization through `StringTypeOptions`, available via both
`p.string(options)` and configured `StringType` instances.

Normalization is applied consistently during database conversion, hydration,
and query parameter conversion. Direct assignment, `em.create()`, and
`em.assign()` retain their existing in-memory semantics.

`p.string()` without options keeps the existing fast path, no universal
property-builder methods are added, and the type benchmarks show no regression.

v1.18.1 — June 21, 2026

This release focuses on Node HTTP adapter fixes, safer AxiosError serialisation, runtime/type correctness fixes, documentation updates, and dependency maintenance.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • AxiosError Serialisation: Made AxiosError#cause non-enumerable to prevent circular JSON serialisation failures when errors include nested causes. (#10913)
  • Node HTTP Adapter: Guarded socket.setKeepAlive for proxy agent streams, accepted path-only URLs when socketPath is configured, deferred environment proxy handling to Node, and explicitly passed maxBodyLength through to follow-redirects. (#10917, #10930, #10942, #10993)
  • Runtime and Type Correctness: Fixed several runtime crashes, type definition mismatches, and incorrect error handling paths. (#10959, #11021)
  • AxiosURLSearchParams: Switched the encoder callback to an arrow function so encoder.call(this) receives the AxiosURLSearchParams instance correctly. (#11019)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Documentation: Documented sensitive headers and status transition behaviour, prepared cleaned-up docs, added Deno install instructions, and clarified that request data is request-specific (#11007, #11010, #11023, #11025)

  • Dependencies: Bumped vite, rollup, form-data, js-yaml, and multer across the root project, docs, smoke tests, and module test workspaces. (#11011, #11012, #11013, #11014, #11015, #11016, #11017, #11026)

🔒 Security Fixes

items.title: ci: pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs
items.body:
CI supply-chain hardening: every third-party action in all four workflow files (`tests.yml`, `release.yml`, `docs.yml`, `codeql-analysis.yml`) is now pinned to a full commit SHA, with the resolved version kept as a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move after review; a SHA can't. Renovate understands the `sha # vX.Y.Z` convention and bumps the digest and comment together.

The original PR pinned the three mutable-ref usages (`crate-ci/typos@master` twice, `apify/workflows/execute-workflow@main` in the release-dispatch job). The maintainer follow-up commits extend the same treatment to the remaining actions (checkout, setup-node, codeql-action, setup-deno, codecov, cpu-cores, the Pages actions) and bump the pins to current: typos v1.49.0 and the latest `apify/workflows` main. All other pinned SHAs already match each action's latest release, so behavior is unchanged.

Thanks @kobihikri for kicking this off.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. items.body:
The `@mikro-orm/cli needs to be installed as a local dependency!` check reads `dependencies`/`devDependencies` from `package.json`. Detect Deno via `process.versions.deno` and skip the heuristic — same pattern already used for `process.versions.bun` elsewhere in the file.

Closes #7766

items.title: feat(pglite): add PGlite driver
items.body:
## Summary

Adds `@mikro-orm/pglite`, a PostgreSQL driver backed by [PGlite](https://pglite.dev) (Postgres-in-WASM) using kysely 0.29's native `PGliteDialect`. No `pg`, no Docker, no server — just an embedded Postgres that runs in Node, Bun, Deno, and the browser.

To make the new driver thin and avoid pulling `pg` into pglite users' dependency graph, this PR pushes everything postgres-but-not-`pg`-specific from `@mikro-orm/postgresql` down into `@mikro-orm/sql`. After the refactor, `@mikro-orm/postgresql` shrinks to a connection-only wrapper around `pg`/`pg-cursor`, and `@mikro-orm/pglite` consumes the shared base classes.

Three commits, reviewable independently:

1. **`chore(deps): update kysely to 0.29.0`** — bumps all 8 driver packages from 0.28.17 to 0.29.0 stable, and updates the dataloader snapshot (kysely 0.29 changes flush timing for parallel `Promise.all` queries; the SQL is identical, only array order shifts).

2. **`refactor(sql): consolidate postgres-shared platform helpers`** — moves `escape` (with `escapeLiteral` inlined from libpq, no `pg` dep), `parseDate`, `convertInterval{To,From}JSValue`, and `unmarshallArray` (`postgres-array`) into `BasePostgreSqlPlatform`. New `BasePostgreSqlEntityManager` (carries `refreshMaterializedView`) and `typeOverrides.ts` (single source of truth for the date/timestamp/timestamptz/interval OID parsers). The shared `raw` helper now does the `$N → ?` rewrite for compiled kysely queries — harmless for sqlite/mysql/mssql, so the postgres-only variant in `@mikro-orm/postgresql` is no longer needed. `PostgreSqlPlatform` and `PostgreSqlEntityManager` stay as empty subclasses for type identity / public API stability. `postgres-array`/`postgres-date`/`postgres-interval` deps move from `postgresql` to `sql`.

3. **`feat(pglite): new driver based on kysely's PGliteDialect`** — the new package. `PgliteSchemaHelper` no-ops the CREATE/DROP DATABASE lifecycle (single-database engine), `PglitePlatform` reports `supportsMultipleStatements()` as false (extended query protocol = one statement per `query()`), `PgliteConnection` lazy-builds the `PGlite` instance and overrides `executeDump` to use `pglite.exec()` for multi-statement schema dumps. `PgliteMikroORM` extends `SqlMikroORM` (the shared base in `@mikro-orm/sql`), matching every other driver. `definePgliteConfig` defaults `dbName` to `memory://` so users don't need to spell out the in-memory case; `dbName` is forwarded to PGlite's `dataDir`, so `idb://name` (browser), a filesystem path, or omitting it (memory) all work without new core options.

## Notes

- Streaming is intentionally not implemented — kysely's PGliteDriver throws `Streaming is not supported by PGlite.` which we let propagate. Use `@mikro-orm/postgresql` if you need cursor-based streaming.
- `tests/tsconfig.json` enables `skipLibCheck` because PGlite's `.d.ts` references DOM/Emscripten ambient globals that aren't in this project's TS lib.
- The driver does **not** auto-create a missing `dataDir` — matches current v7 sqlite behavior. Auto-mkdir parity for both drivers can be tackled separately on master.

```
    at eval (eval at createFunction (file:///.../mikro-orm/packages/core/src/utils/Utils.ts:900:14), <anonymous>:13:68)
    at ChangeSetComputer.computePayload (file:///.../mikro-orm/packages/core/src/unit-of-work/ChangeSetComputer.ts:145:20)
    at ChangeSetComputer.computeChangeSet (file:///.../mikro-orm/packages/core/src/unit-of-work/ChangeSetComputer.ts:61:56)
    at UnitOfWork.findNewEntities (file:///.../mikro-orm/packages/core/src/unit-of-work/UnitOfWork.ts:780:46)
    at UnitOfWork.computeChangeSets (file:///.../mikro-orm/packages/core/src/unit-of-work/UnitOfWork.ts:634:12)
    at UnitOfWork.doCommit (file:///.../mikro-orm/packages/core/src/unit-of-work/UnitOfWork.ts:514:12)
```

## Investigation

Why is this bug appearing with Deno? The behavior is different because of [this line of code in the `bson` package](https://github.com/mongodb/js-bson/blob/0712bb15653093766a80bbd4ba104353cd4581e3/src/utils/byte_utils.ts#L69):
- with Node.js, `Buffer.prototype?._isBuffer` is `undefined` ; so `ByteUtils` is using `nodeJsByteUtils`
- with Deno, `Buffer.prototype?._isBuffer` is `true` ; so `ByteUtils` is using `webByteUtils`

The content of the `fromHex` method is different in both implementations:
- With `nodeJsByteUtils`, [it uses `Buffer.from`](https://github.com/mongodb/js-bson/blob/0712bb15653093766a80bbd4ba104353cd4581e3/src/utils/node_byte_utils.ts#L150)
- with `webByteUtils`, [it uses `Uint8Array.from`](https://github.com/mongodb/js-bson/blob/0712bb15653093766a80bbd4ba104353cd4581e3/src/utils/web_byte_utils.ts#L258)

The issue is that our `clone` function in `packages/core/src/utils/clone.ts` does not handle cloning of `Uint8Array` properly.

For instance, whit the following `Uint8Array` array:
```
Uint8Array(12) [
  105, 172, 10
]
```
Cloning it with our util function will result in:
```
Uint8Array {
  "0": 105,
  "1": 172,
  "2": 10
}
```

## Fix

In this PR, we add proper support for cloning [all `TypedArray` subtypes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray#typedarray_objects).

items.title: MikroORM v7
items.body:
Check the upgrading guide at https://github.com/mikro-orm/mikro-orm/blob/v7/docs/docs/upgrading-v6-to-v7.md

## Remove dependency on knex

I already started refactoring the ORM QB to remove this dependency in favor of manual query building. We already did a lot on our own to workaround knex issues, so this feels like a natural step. 

Using query builders like knex or kysely will still be possible, but from outside (install them explicitly). Support for raw queries will be exclusively handled via the `raw` helper, and we might provide some plugins to map knex/kysely instances to the `raw` helper, or something similar.

I still don't have a clear vision of how this will end up, but removing all the tight coupling is the first step which I already started working on. Some of those changes (mainly in the schema generator) can be done in a non breaking way, which I hope to do during the v6 lifecycle. We might as well end up with `@mikro-orm/knex` and `@mikro-orm/kysely` packages, but the internals won't depend on them anyhow, using those packages will be optional. Most of the code we currently have in `@mikro-orm/knex` would live in a new package like `@mikro-orm/sql`.

✅ #6400

## ESM only

I'd like to convert the project to native ESM (and move to vitest). Given the recent addition of `require(esm)` support in node (which was also backported to node 20), I hope it will be enough to provide the ESM build instead of dealing with dual builds and possible dual package hazard, which is a real problem for us, we use global state for decorator metadata. Node 23 unflags the `require(esm)` feature.

I will definitely provide the CJS build too if this should be a problem, on the other hand, if the `require(esm)` will just work, I don't see a real reason to deal with the dual builds. This won't mean that you need to move to ESM.

✅ #6403

## New ~hybrid~ balanced loading strategy

We have two loading strategies right now: select-in and joined. Both have their pros and cons. The main issue with the joined strategy is the potentially huge cartesian product of the rows you can get because of joining to-many relations. I'd like to have a new hybrid strategy as the default in v7, which would join to-one relations (m:1 and 1:1) but use separate queries for to-many relations (1:m and m:n). That way, we shouldn't end up with the cartesian products at all, while using just one query for the to-one joins. This is technically already possible if you use the joined strategy and override it on your collection properties.

✅ #6787

## Native support for streaming

Streaming always required going raw with knex, and v7 should finally change that. I'd like to have `em.stream` and `qb.stream` user-facing methods, that will support both row-by-row streaming, as well as batched yields of complete root entity graphs (dealing with the cartesian product from to-many relations).

Streaming will not manipulate the identity map, only place where identity will be ensured is in the context of a single root entity record (so its relations will only contain a single entity instance).

✅ #6923

## Auto flush mode

The current default is auto flush, which means every find call first checks for dirty items in the context which could affect the results, and flush if there are any. While this default means stronger consistency, it also brings a performance penalty.

The mechanism behind the dirty checking works based on get/set scalar properties (we already use this for relations to support propagation, and that is going to stay as is). Having all the scalars redefined as get/set is adding quite a perf hit when you want to work with a large number of entities. Right now, if you globally disable the auto flush mode, the scalar properties wont be redefined this way, but we can leave this up to the user if they call `em.persist` on the entity (even if its managed already), we could schedule a dirty check for the auto flush mode to get around this.

✅ #6982

## Defaults in EntityGenerator

A lot has changed in the EntityGenerator over the past years. It is a powerful tool that covers many use cases, but the defaults are still unchanged. In v7, I'd like to change the defaults so we emit entity definitions with `defineEntity` and enums in the `dictionary` mode. Specifically, this is the new set of defaults I am considering now:

```ts
entityDefinition: 'defineEntity',
enumMode: 'dictionary',
bidirectionalRelations: true,
identifiedReferences: true,
```

✅ #6984

## More TypeScript loaders in CLI

TS support was provided natively via ts-node, which seems to be dead nowadays, it didn't survive the ESM-related changes in Node. Next version will allow using different TS loaders automatically, just install one of `swc`, `tsx`, `jiti`, or `tsimp` and things should work.

✅ #6987

## Zero dependencies in the core package

All dependencies were dropped from the core package:

- #7005 
- #7006
- #7007
- #7008
- #7011

## ES decorators

All decorators are now moved to a new `@mikro-orm/decorators` package, and provided in two variants:

- To use legacy decorators, import them from `@mikro-orm/decorators/legacy`:

	```ts
	import { Entity, PrimaryKey, Property } from '@mikro-orm/decorators/legacy';
	```

- To use ES spec decorators, import them from `@mikro-orm/decorators/es`:

	```ts
	import { Entity, PrimaryKey, Property } from '@mikro-orm/decorators/es';
	```

Note that ES decorators don't support metadata reflection, you need to provide scalar property types explicitly.

✅ #7011

## No direct dependency on Node.js

The runtime (core + drivers) no longer depends on `node` imports like `node:path` or `node:fs`, making it easier to bundle, and setting a baseline for potential support on deno and other runtimes. There are still some not-so-optional dependencies, like `AsyncLocalStorage`, that have a dummy fallback, so it's possible to build the project, but some features won't work correctly (e.g. concurrent flush).

This will set a baseline for potential deployment to deno or JSR.

The following packages still depend on Node.js runtime:

- `@mikro-orm/cli`
- `@mikro-orm/migrations` (+`@mikro-orm/migrations-mongodb`)
- `@mikro-orm/seeder`
- `@mikro-orm/entity-generator`
- `@mikro-orm/migrations`
- `@mikro-orm/reflection`

✅ #7021

## Improved support for minification

Previously, a lot of internals depended on the entity class name, but some bundlers like to mangle class names, and some even don't care about the uniqueness of those names. We used to validate against this, enforcing people to disable class name mangling. With v7, a class reference is now used internally instead of the class name, making it resistant to duplicity in entity class names. Note that there are still places where we rely on the class names (e.g. STI).

✅ #7067

## Changes in docs

Speaking of the `defineEntity` helper, it should become the preferred way all over the docs, and all the examples should use it (via code tabs, showing the decorators too, but as an alternative instead). The current getting started guide has a lot of stuff around edge cases with decorators and ts-morph, those parts make it feel like the ORM is hard to use, we should show the happy path instead, how to get to a working project soon, in a way that will work fine with modern approaches like running TS via node.

✅ #7088

## Others

- [x] require node 22 lts
- [x] swap the default of `embeddables.prefixMode` to `relative`
- [x] remove `qb.then` method (disable awaitability of the QB instances) #4876
- [x] map arrays inside object embeddables to JSON arrays by default
- [x] #6974
- [x] change signature of `em.addFilter()` to use a single options object
- [x] change default propagation to `REQUIRED` in `@Transactional` decorator
- [x] #7018
- [x] #7020
- [x] #7058
- [x] #7090
- [ ] #6704

Closes #6116
